title: New luminescent Zn(II) compound as a highly select
one_line_summary: [Zn3(3-atrz)2(4-atrz)2(SO4)2] shows thermal_stability = 322.0 K for target gas

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: electron transfer from framework conduction band to Fe3+ half-filled 3d orbital → selectivity

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: 3-atrz adopts μ3-N1,N2,N3 coordination and 4-atrz adopts μ2-N1,N2 coordination in the 3D framework → stability

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] use two isomorphic aminotriazole ligands together with sulfate to bridge trinuclear Zn(II) subunits → forms a 3D framework with 6-connected pcu topology

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] rationally design and construct MOFs with intense luminescence → supports selective and sensitive detection of Fe3+ ions

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: compound 1 vs previously reported MOFs not based on two different isomorphic aminotriazole ligands: winner=subject_a on novelty_and_combined_Fe3+_sensing_luminescence_performance

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: compound 1 vs free 4-atrz ligand: winner=tie on emission_peak_position_under_340_nm_excitation

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] further heat the framework beyond its stable temperature range: the framework of compound 1 collapses

notable_quotes: Compound 1 selectively detects Fe3+ in water via strong luminescence quenching; emission is completely quenched at 0.923 nM Fe3+.
Compound 1 forms a trinuclear-subunit 3D framework that simplifies to a 6-connected pcu topology.
A new Zn(II) MOF, [Zn3(3-atrz)2(4-atrz)2(SO4)2]n, was solvothermally synthesized from ZnSO4·7H2O with 3-atrz and 4-atrz, giving yellow block crystals in 32% yield.
